factors.name: Connector branching / arc density
factors.summary: Very high loadings (0.86–0.97) of average and maximum connector degree, token split, arcs per node and control flow complexity show that this factor captures how many arcs connectors carry, i.e. the branching and connectivity of the net. Number of empty sequence flows (0.75, also 0.43 on Factor 3) and Connector Mismatch (0.56, also 0.38 on Factor 4) load more moderately. Size also loads 0.45 here besides its main loading on Factor 2.

factors.name: Size and separability
factors.summary: Size (0.85) and Separability (0.82) load together, so larger nets in this dataset also tend to have a higher share of non-articulation nodes. Sequentiality also has a moderate loading (0.50), although it is assigned to Factor 3. The factor rests on two measures only.

factors.name: Sequentiality / connector mix
factors.summary: Sequentiality (0.79) and Connector Heterogeneity (0.66) define this factor, with a secondary loading of Number of empty sequence flows (0.43). Its exact meaning is unclear: it links a high share of non-connector arcs with a more even mix of parallel and choice connectors. Connector Heterogeneity has a modest communality (0.46).

factors.name: Weak residual factor
factors.summary: No measure is assigned to this factor; the largest loadings are Connector Mismatch (0.38) and Maximum connector degree (0.28), and it explains only 2.6% of variance. It should not be interpreted substantively.

interpretation.overall: The data are suitable for factor analysis (Bartlett p < 0.001, KMO 0.81). Four varimax-rotated factors explain 86% of variance, but the eigenvalues and the suggested number of factors (2) indicate that two to three factors suffice. A dominant connector branching/connectivity factor (50% of variance) is followed by a size/separability factor and a weaker sequentiality/connector-mix factor, while the fourth factor is essentially empty. Density was removed by the MSA filter and Number of duplicate tasks was constant, so neither is represented.
caveats: Four factors were extracted although only two were suggested, so Factor 4 (and possibly Factor 3) is likely overfactoring.
Coefficient of network connectivity shows a possible Heywood case (communality near 1), which may distort the solution.

Several measures have substantial secondary loadings (e.g. Size 0.45 on Factor 1, Sequentiality 0.50 on Factor 2, Number of empty sequence flows 0.43 on Factor 3), so the factors are not cleanly separated.
Density and Number of duplicate tasks were excluded, so the factors do not cover them.
The results reflect shared variance in these 288 discovered nets and depend on the discovery algorithms, rotation and number of factors; they do not imply causal structure.
